hero.headline: TCCEED expands paid summer internship program with 61 student placements across Treasure Coast
hero.body:
TCCEED expanded its paid summer internship program in its second year, doubling employer participation and placing 61 students in local jobs across the Treasure Coast. The initiative saw applications from Treasure Coast students triple compared to the previous year.

The program connects local students with paid internship opportunities at businesses and organizations throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties. Employer participation doubled from the first year of the program, providing more opportunities for students to gain work experience.

The tripling of student applications indicates growing awareness and interest in the program among Treasure Coast youth. The 61 placements represent students working in various sectors across the three-county region this summer.

TCCEED operates the workforce development initiative as part of its mission to prepare local students for careers in the Treasure Coast economy. The program provides students with both income and professional experience during the summer months.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman accused of using vehicle to assault three people
cards.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, is being held in the St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond after being accused of using a vehicle as a weapon to assault three people. She faces three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

The arrest occurred in St. Lucie County, though specific details about the location and circumstances of the alleged assault have not been released by authorities. Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon is a serious felony charge in Florida.

Hines remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail. The $75,000 bond reflects the severity of the charges, which involve the alleged use of a vehicle as a deadly weapon against multiple victims.

The case involves three separate counts, one for each alleged victim in the incident. Each count of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon carries significant potential prison time under Florida law.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida Home Insurance Market Shows Signs of Recovery as Carriers Return, Rates Decline
cards.body:
Florida's troubled home insurance market is displaying signs of stabilization as more insurance carriers return to the state and some policyholders see rate reductions. The shift marks a potential turning point for homeowners who have faced years of escalating premiums and limited coverage options.

Insurance companies are re-entering the Florida market after a prolonged exodus that left many property owners scrambling for coverage. The return of additional carriers is creating more competition in a market that had become increasingly concentrated among a shrinking number of providers. Some insurers are now offering lower rates to Florida homeowners, a reversal from the double-digit increases that have characterized recent years.

The improvement comes as Florida's insurance crisis had reached critical levels, with numerous carriers withdrawing from the state due to hurricane losses and litigation costs. Many homeowners had been forced into the state-backed Citizens Property Insurance Corporation, which serves as the insurer of last resort. The stabilization of the private market could reduce strain on Citizens and provide property owners with more choices for coverage.

The recovery remains fragile and uneven across the state. While some areas and policyholders are benefiting from increased competition and declining rates, others continue to face high premiums and limited options. The long-term stability of Florida's insurance market will depend on continued carrier participation and the state's exposure to future hurricane seasons. Industry observers are monitoring whether the improvements will hold as the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season progresses through its peak months.

cards.headline: Florida Homeowner Without Insurance Faces Repair Bills After Hurricane Milton Destroys Roof
cards.teaser: A Florida man who paid off his house found himself facing major repair costs just two months later when Hurricane Milton tore off his roof.
cards.body:
A Florida homeowner is confronting significant repair bills after Hurricane Milton damaged his property just two months after he finished paying off his mortgage. The storm tore off the roof of his house, leaving him with extensive damage and no insurance coverage to help with costs.

The homeowner had been living without home insurance when the hurricane struck, forcing him to pay for all repairs out of pocket. The timing proved particularly difficult, coming immediately after he had achieved the milestone of owning his home free and clear. He is now responsible for the full cost of replacing the roof and repairing any additional damage caused by the storm.

The case highlights the risks facing Florida homeowners who go without insurance coverage in a state frequently threatened by hurricanes and severe weather. Many property owners have dropped coverage or been unable to afford policies as rates have climbed in recent years.

cards.headline: Park Vista Football Team Eyes State Playoffs After Strong 2025 Finish
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said the team felt good throughout the second half of that season. The team is working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, and Bender said all the pieces are in place now, it's just about executing. Senior Erik Lee said coming in, he feels like the team has the guys needed to get it done, but they also have to put the work in to get there as well.

The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017. Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. Hanna said the team has to handle business weekly, and if they do that and do their job, that will get them in the playoffs. Senior Justice Jones said it is going to feel amazing, because he already knows it is going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Treasure Coast shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
cards.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes
cards.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year, prompting more households to adjust their purchasing decisions based on price rather than preference. For shoppers looking to stretch their dollars, the discount grocer offers an alternative to traditional supermarkets at a time when food costs continue to climb.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. Cheryl said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "They're the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what's on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that," she said. The changing shopping habits reflect a broader trend as more households look for ways to manage rising food costs.

Price movements in key grocery categories show a mixed picture for consumers. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Despite some declining categories, the overall trajectory points to continued upward pressure on grocery bills.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated and are not gonna go down," they said, adding they would be willing to bet on that. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase," they said. The new location gives Treasure Coast residents another option for managing household budgets as inflation continues to impact the cost of food.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova Ends Coco Gauff's Wimbledon Run in Dramatic Tiebreaker
hero.teaser: Muchova defeated Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) on Thursday to become the fourth Czech woman in six years to reach the Wimbledon final.
hero.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova Wins Wimbledon After Recovering From Blown Match Points
cards.teaser: The 21-year-old Czech player overcame Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in Saturday's final for her first Grand Slam trophy.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova is the latest in a long line of Czech women to win Wimbledon. The 21-year-old Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy.

Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was the greatest Czech-born player of them all, Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club.

Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Justin Bieber, Madonna Join Star-Studded World Cup Final Halftime Show
cards.teaser: Justin Bieber will join headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS for the 11-minute halftime performance during the July 19 final outside New York.
cards.body:
Justin Bieber will bring his swag to the World Cup's star-studded, Super Bowl-style halftime show, joining fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS, FIFA announced Wednesday. Afrobeats star Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus, a choir of elementary school students based in Staten Island, New York, will also perform, the last joined by Coldplay. The 11-minute halftime performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin, will take place during the final outside New York on July 19. The show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which is raising $100 million to help children access education and soccer. Bieber said in a statement that the FIFA World Cup brings the world together in a way nothing else can, and he is grateful to be part of the halftime show and knowing it's already helping expand access to education for children around the world.

Of all the performances, the addition of Burna Boy is particularly noteworthy. He is one-half of this year's official song for the World Cup, "Dai Dai," led by Shakira. The song is a mesh of their musical landscapes: Afrobeats and Latin rhythms, an undeniably global, multilingual pop track. In one verse, they name a number of the world's most famous soccer players and countries competing in this year's World Cup: "Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Colombia," Shakira cheers. "Mexico, Japan, Korea, Netherlands." This year's World Cup halftime performance will also feature some characters from "Sesame Street," as well as Muppets like Kermit and Miss Piggy.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
hero.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club
hero.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company.

When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, Rosario Liz's reaction was immediate. "I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box. Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said.

He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," he said.

He closed with a message for younger members at the club. "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now," Rosario Liz said. The recognition as a flag bearer comes after his selection as Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region, one of the highest honors given by the Boys & Girls Clubs of America. As one of only 12 club members chosen nationally for this role, Rosario Liz will represent not only his local club in St. Lucie County but also youth organizations across the country at the World Cup finals.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with panoramic views
hero.teaser: Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top rewards visitors with breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The striking red brick tower continues to serve as both a historic landmark and an active attraction, drawing visitors who want to experience its rich history and spectacular views. The 105-step climb follows a narrow spiral staircase that lighthouse keepers once climbed night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that illuminated the waters for mariners navigating below. Each step connects modern visitors to the keepers who dedicated their lives to guiding ships safely along Florida's treacherous coastline, offering a glimpse into the daily routine of those who maintained this vital navigational aid through the decades.

Reaching the gallery at the top rewards visitors with breathtaking panoramic views in every direction. The Atlantic Ocean stretches endlessly to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel as the sea breeze sweeps across the observation deck, making even warm Florida mornings feel comfortable. The vantage point provides a unique perspective on the surrounding waterways and coastline that mariners have relied upon for over a century and a half.

After descending from the tower, visitors can explore the museum grounds and restored historic buildings that tell the story of the lighthouse's fascinating past. The exhibits cover the lighthouse's construction before the Civil War, a tumultuous period in American history when this beacon first began its service. The displays also detail the lighthouse's years as an active Coast Guard station, highlighting the evolution of lighthouse keeping and maritime safety over the generations.

The combination of climbing the working lighthouse and exploring the museum grounds offers a comprehensive look at how this structure has served the Florida coast for more than 165 years. The experience provides both an educational journey through maritime history and a memorable visit for anyone seeking the spectacular views from the top of the red brick tower. The lighthouse stands as a testament to the keepers who carried the weight of history with every footfall as they performed their duties protecting ships along the coastline.
